title: The algebra of the nonnegative cone of an integral basis
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ an additive abelian group, $r\in\mathbf N$, and $(u_i)_{i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}}$ an integral basis of $G$, meaning that every $g\in G$ has a unique expression $g=\sum_i n_i u_i$ with $n_i\in\mathbf Z$. Define the additive submonoid $H\subseteq G$ generated by the $u_i$, equivalently $H=\{\sum_i a_i u_i:a_i\in\mathbf N\}$. For $T=H$ or $G$, use the additive monoid algebra $k[T]=\bigoplus_{t\in T}ke^t$, whose multiplication is $e^t e^{t\prime}=e^{t+t\prime}$. Define the basis monomial $x_i=e^{u_i}\in k[H]$. Define $\iota:k[H]\to k[G]$ by extension of coefficients by zero outside $H$; it is the $k$-algebra homomorphism induced by the submonoid inclusion $H\hookrightarrow G$. This includes $r=0$, with the empty family, $G=H=\{0\}$, and the constant-monomial inclusion.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.12 proof, printed pp.104--105: the lattice group algebra and freely generated positive monoid; explicit basis-cone specialization used in the polynomial and localization calculations.
